title: Christ suffered so the repentant need not suffer
setting: Martin Harris was a prosperous farmer near Palmyra, New York. He had agreed to pay the Palmyra printer Egbert Grandin to print the Book of Mormon. Grandin’s price for five thousand copies was $3,000, nearly all of Harris’s property. This revelation, given through Joseph Smith at Manchester, urged Harris to pay. On 25 August 1829 Harris mortgaged his farm to Grandin. Early printings dated the revelation March 1830, but historians now favor summer 1829.
summary: The revelation opens with the speaker naming himself Alpha and Omega, Christ the Lord. It says every person must repent or suffer. It explains that “endless” and “eternal” punishment mean God’s punishment, because Endless is his name. It commands Martin Harris to repent, describing Christ’s own suffering that made him bleed at every pore. It tells Harris to preach only repentance for now. It commands him not to covet his property but to pay for printing the Book of Mormon. It tells him to pray aloud as well as in secret and to declare glad tidings. It ends by telling him to pay the printer, release himself from bondage, and come to Christ.

contextNote.title: Suffering that was meant to be spared
contextNote.text: Harris was asked to risk his farm, and the revelation answers with a lesson about suffering. Verse 16 says God has “suffered these things for all” so they need not suffer if they repent. Verse 17 states the other side: those who do not repent must suffer as he did. Verse 18 then describes that suffering as pain that made him tremble and bleed at every pore. Verse 19 says he finished it anyway. Set against verse 26, Harris’s loss of property looks small. In this passage, Christ’s suffering is offered as a substitute that repentance accepts.

ldsText: The 2025 Come, Follow Me lesson for section 19, “Learn of Me,” focuses on the Savior’s suffering and the peace He offers through repentance. Verse 23 invites Harris to “learn of me” and find peace; what do verses 16–19 teach you about why repentance brings peace?
reviewNote: Read all 41 verses. Official heading gives Manchester, likely summer 1829, to Martin Harris. JSP historical introduction read for the date debate (March 1830 in 1833 and 1835 printings vs. summer 1829), Grandin’s $3,000 price, and the 25 August 1829 mortgage. Month set to 1829-07 as a best estimate between June negotiations and the August mortgage; the exact month is unknown. Fact-check 2026-10-12: grammar fix in ldsText question (“what do verses”). Setting facts confirmed against JSP.
